notes: Why this course exists: the owner's Five Frames notebook produced a seven-cluster outline (2026-11-16); scanned against 352 sessions, five clusters are on tape and two (Munger's lattice, the Army acronyms) are not. This plan carries the on-tape ones in Ken's own windows: (1) the brain builds a model (t4NkztDo_tc, Ken alone, 16 min, 'it takes one slide'); (2) systems thinking (the YRQLU1w_77A interview: definition, feedback loop, structure+process, 80/20 science/art, the meta-system); (3) the chimp (Celia, rJg6jv24s20; Tom's line, B9HVuTtPVqM); (4) plan-prepare-execute-assess with the daily AAR (fbk3g-UCSkc) and the detect-decide-deliver-assess drill-down (muuwye8ozpQ). Not carried: Munger (0 hits in the corpus; the 'inversion' hits are yield curves), FFTC, D3A's 'battle drill with zero-thinking friction' wording, 'flow state' (7 passing mentions), law of large numbers (6 passing mentions). Off-tape clusters belong in the written companion under their own authors' names. Running time about 38 min with the three optional segments off (s07, s13, s30); the shortest honest cut is Ch1 + Ch4 at ~18 min. Speaker permission: Tom Hardison (s22) and Bill Scheidt's questions (s10, s12 lead-ins) are not Ken. Order can flip: Ch2 (systems) before Ch1 (brain) if the owner wants the market before the trader.
